evaluations.prompt: which PyTorch operator is launching the slow GPU kernels in my model?
expected_behavior: lists the captured operators with --experimental --list-operators torch
checks the documented PyTorch version requirement
unexpected_behavior: guesses an operator pattern without listing the captured operators first

evaluations.prompt: profile my training script and tell me which layer the GPU time belongs to
expected_behavior: profiles the Python script with --experimental --trace-ml-api torch
advises profiling a few steady-state iterations rather than a full run

evaluations.prompt: my model uses torch.compile, how do I attribute the generated Triton kernels?
expected_behavior: uses --experimental --trace-ml-api torch, because --trace-ml-api triton does not capture kernels that torch.compile generates
unexpected_behavior: relies on --trace-ml-api triton alone to capture torch.compile kernels

evaluations.prompt: show me the counters for just the relu operators in this traced PyTorch workload
expected_behavior: treats the pattern as a shell-style glob rather than a regex
unexpected_behavior: passes --list-operators and --operator on the same command

evaluations.prompt: I added my own ROCTx ranges in my Python script. Profile it and show the GPU work inside that region.
expected_behavior: lists the user region with --experimental --list-operators user
shows the operator call tree under that region, including nested ML API operators and the GPU kernels they launched

evaluations.prompt: attribute GPU kernels to functions in my compiled C++ HIP binary
expected_behavior: says that operator attribution requires a Python workload and cannot annotate a compiled binary
offers kernel filtering with -k or dispatch filtering with -d instead
unexpected_behavior: claims --trace-ml-api can attribute kernels to functions in a compiled binary
